questiontext.text: In the context of large language models, what is a token?

answer.text: A sub-word unit that text is split into before being processed by the model

feedback.text: Correct — tokenisation breaks text into smaller units (whole words, sub-words, or characters) that the model processes numerically.

answer.text: A complete sentence used as input to the model

feedback.text: Incorrect — tokens are much smaller than sentences; a sentence typically contains many tokens.

answer.text: A binary value representing whether a word is present or absent

feedback.text: Incorrect — tokens are mapped to dense embedding vectors, not binary presence/absence indicators.

answer.text: A random number assigned to each word for encryption

feedback.text: Incorrect — tokenisation is a deterministic process for converting text into numerical units, not encryption.

name.text: Q: What does encoder-free mean for Gemma 4 12B?

questiontext.text: When Gemma 4 12B is described as "encoder-free," what does this mean?

answer.text: It has no separate vision or audio encoder networks — raw inputs are projected directly into the LLM's embedding space

feedback.text: Correct — the dedicated vision encoder (550M params) and audio encoder (305M params) are replaced with lightweight linear projections.

answer.text: It cannot process images or audio at all

feedback.text: Incorrect — Gemma 4 12B supports text, image, AND audio inputs despite having no dedicated encoders.

answer.text: It uses an encoder-decoder architecture instead of a decoder-only one

feedback.text: Incorrect — Gemma 4 12B is decoder-only in its core architecture AND encoder-free in its multimodal processing.

answer.text: It does not use the attention mechanism

feedback.text: Incorrect — the LLM's 48 decoder layers use attention extensively; it is the separate modality-specific encoders that are removed.

questiontext.text: Approximately how many parameters does Gemma 4 12B's vision embedder have, and what is the primary source of those parameters?

answer.text: 35 million, mostly from the linear projection matrix that converts 6,912 pixel values to 3,840-dimensional embeddings

feedback.text: Correct — the projection matrix alone is 6,912 × 3,840 ≈ 26M parameters, accounting for most of the 35M total.

answer.text: 550 million, from 27 layers of transformer attention

feedback.text: Incorrect — 550M is the size of the traditional vision encoder used in Gemma 4 31B, not the lightweight embedder in 12B.

answer.text: 35 million, from multiple layers of convolutional neural networks

feedback.text: Incorrect — the embedder uses a single linear projection, not convolutional layers.

answer.text: 305 million, from conformer layers processing image patches

feedback.text: Incorrect — 305M is the audio encoder size in E2B/E4B models, not the vision embedder.

answer.text: Raw 16 kHz audio is sliced into 40ms frames of 640 values each, then each frame is linearly projected to the LLM's embedding dimension

feedback.text: Correct — this is the entire audio pipeline: slice and project. No tokenisation, no conformer layers.

answer.text: Audio is converted to a spectrogram image and processed by the vision embedder

feedback.text: Incorrect — audio is processed as raw amplitude samples, not converted to images.

answer.text: Audio is transcribed to text first, then the text is processed normally

feedback.text: Incorrect — the model processes raw audio waveforms directly, not pre-transcribed text.

answer.text: Audio is processed through 12 conformer layers before reaching the LLM

feedback.text: Incorrect — that is how E2B and E4B process audio. Gemma 4 12B skips all conformer layers entirely.

questiontext.text: How does Gemma 4 12B encode the spatial position of image patches without a vision encoder?

answer.text: Two learned matrices (X and Y) provide coordinate-based positional embeddings that are summed and added to each patch embedding

feedback.text: Correct — the factorised X/Y lookup system provides spatial information without requiring attention-based 2D-RoPE.

answer.text: Standard 1D positional encoding from the LLM is used since images are flattened into sequences

feedback.text: Incorrect — 1D encoding cannot represent 2D spatial relationships in images; the separate X/Y matrices are needed.

answer.text: 2D Rotary Position Encoding (2D-RoPE) is applied within the embedder's attention layers

feedback.text: Incorrect — the embedder has no attention layers, so 2D-RoPE cannot be used. This is why the X/Y matrix approach was developed.

answer.text: No positional encoding is needed because the patch order is sufficient

feedback.text: Incorrect — without positional information, the model would not know where patches are located in the original image.

questiontext.text: What two types of attention does Gemma 4 12B interleave in its 48 decoder layers?

answer.text: Local sliding window attention (1,024 tokens) and global full attention (up to 256K tokens)

feedback.text: Correct — local attention handles nearby context efficiently while global attention provides full-context awareness at key points.

answer.text: Self-attention and cross-attention between encoder and decoder

feedback.text: Incorrect — there is no encoder to cross-attend to. Both attention types are self-attention variants within the decoder.

answer.text: Causal attention and bidirectional attention

feedback.text: Incorrect — all attention in a decoder-only model is causal (masked). The distinction is between local and global scope.

answer.text: Multi-head attention and single-head attention alternating between layers

feedback.text: Incorrect — both local and global attention use multi-head attention. The distinction is scope (window size), not head count.

questiontext.text: Why is fine-tuning Gemma 4 12B simpler than fine-tuning traditional multimodal models?

answer.text: All modalities share the same weights, so a single fine-tuning pass updates text, image, and audio understanding together

feedback.text: Correct — without separate frozen encoders, LoRA or full fine-tuning naturally updates the entire multimodal pipeline in one pass.

answer.text: The model has fewer parameters, so fine-tuning is faster

feedback.text: Incorrect — while fewer total parameters helps, the key advantage is architectural: no separate encoder to co-tune.

answer.text: Fine-tuning is not needed because the model already works perfectly for all domains

feedback.text: Incorrect — domain-specific fine-tuning remains valuable for specialised applications like medical imaging or technical audio.

answer.text: The model uses a special fine-tuning API that other models do not support

feedback.text: Incorrect — the advantage is architectural, not API-based. Standard tools like HuggingFace and Unsloth are used.

questiontext.text: What is the approximate minimum VRAM needed to run Gemma 4 12B locally at full precision?

answer.text: 16GB

feedback.text: Correct — Gemma 4 12B is specifically designed to fit on consumer GPUs with 16GB of VRAM.

answer.text: 4GB

feedback.text: Incorrect — 4GB is far too little for an 11.95B parameter model at full precision.

answer.text: 80GB

feedback.text: Incorrect — 80GB is what large models (70B+) require. Gemma 4 12B is designed for consumer hardware.

answer.text: 256GB

feedback.text: Incorrect — this far exceeds what Gemma 4 12B needs and is beyond consumer hardware.

questiontext.text: What makes the Gemma 4 26B A4B model run nearly as fast as a 4B model despite having 25.2B total parameters?

answer.text: It uses a Mixture-of-Experts architecture that activates only 3.8B parameters during inference

feedback.text: Correct — the "A4B" stands for "active 4B." Only 8 of 128 experts (plus 1 shared) are active per token.

answer.text: It uses aggressive quantisation to reduce the effective model size

feedback.text: Incorrect — the speed comes from the MoE architecture's sparse activation, not quantisation.

answer.text: It removes most of its layers during inference to speed up processing

feedback.text: Incorrect — all 30 layers are used; the sparsity is in which experts within each layer are activated.

answer.text: It runs on specialised Google hardware that is not available to consumers

feedback.text: Incorrect — the model can run on standard consumer hardware thanks to its efficient MoE design.

questiontext.text: What is the relationship between "decoder-only" and "encoder-free" in the context of Gemma 4?

answer.text: "Decoder-only" refers to the core LLM architecture (no encoder-decoder split); "encoder-free" refers to the absence of separate modality-specific encoders for vision and audio

feedback.text: Correct — these are distinct concepts. All Gemma 4 models are decoder-only, but only the 12B is also encoder-free.

answer.text: They mean exactly the same thing — both indicate the model has no encoder

feedback.text: Incorrect — "decoder-only" is about the core transformer design, while "encoder-free" is about how non-text modalities are handled.

answer.text: "Encoder-free" means the model cannot understand any input, while "decoder-only" means it can only generate output

feedback.text: Incorrect — both encoder-free and decoder-only models can understand inputs; the terms describe architecture, not capability.

answer.text: "Decoder-only" is the older term and "encoder-free" is the modern replacement

feedback.text: Incorrect — these describe different architectural properties that can coexist in the same model.

questiontext.text: What is the primary purpose of the attention mechanism in a transformer?

answer.text: To compute relationships between tokens, allowing each token's representation to incorporate information from other relevant tokens

feedback.text: Correct — attention uses Query, Key, and Value vectors to determine which tokens are relevant to each other and blend their information.

answer.text: To compress the input sequence into a single fixed-size vector

feedback.text: Incorrect — attention preserves the full sequence of tokens rather than compressing to a single vector.

answer.text: To randomly select which tokens to process in order to reduce computation

feedback.text: Incorrect — attention is deterministic and considers all tokens (within its scope), not a random subset.

answer.text: To convert text tokens into image patches for visual processing

feedback.text: Incorrect — attention processes relationships between tokens; it does not convert between modalities.

questiontext.text: What is the purpose of the multi-token prediction (MTP) companion model released alongside Gemma 4 12B?

answer.text: To increase inference speed by predicting multiple tokens per forward pass instead of one at a time

feedback.text: Correct — MTP reduces generation latency by producing several tokens simultaneously, which is especially valuable for local deployment.

answer.text: To train the model faster by processing multiple training examples simultaneously

feedback.text: Incorrect — MTP is an inference optimisation, not a training technique.

answer.text: To translate between multiple languages at the same time

feedback.text: Incorrect — MTP relates to token generation speed, not multilingual capability.

answer.text: To split the model across multiple GPUs for distributed inference

feedback.text: Incorrect — model parallelism is a separate technique. MTP is about predicting more than one token per step.

name.text: TF: Gemma 4 12B is the first medium-sized Gemma model with audio

questiontext.text: Gemma 4 12B is the first medium-sized model in the Gemma family capable of natively processing audio input.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct — previously, audio input was restricted to the smaller E2B and E4B edge models. Gemma 4 12B brings audio to the medium-size tier.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Incorrect — this statement is true. Before the 12B, only the E2B and E4B models supported audio.

name.text: TF: The vision embedder uses attention

questiontext.text: Gemma 4 12B's vision embedder uses multiple layers of attention to process image patches, similar to a Vision Transformer.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Incorrect — the vision embedder has NO attention layers at all. It uses only a single linear projection plus positional embeddings. All attention-based processing happens in the LLM's decoder layers.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Correct — the embedder is entirely attention-free. Each patch is processed in isolation through a linear projection. The LLM handles all attention-based understanding.

name.text: TF: Audio needs special positional encoding

questiontext.text: In Gemma 4 12B, audio input requires special 2D positional embeddings similar to those used for image patches.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Incorrect — audio is inherently a 1D sequential signal, so the LLM's standard positional encoding for sequences applies naturally. Only images need the special X/Y positional embeddings.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Correct — audio frames are sequential, just like text tokens, so they use the LLM's standard positional encoding without any special 2D treatment.

name.text: TF: Gemma 4 models are Apache 2.0 licensed

questiontext.text: All Gemma 4 models are released under the Apache 2.0 open-source license, allowing unrestricted commercial use.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct — Google releases Gemma models under Apache 2.0, enabling both research and commercial deployment without restrictions.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Incorrect — Gemma 4 models are indeed Apache 2.0 licensed.

questiontext.text: Gemma 4 12B supports a context window of up to 256K tokens.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct — the medium-sized models (12B, 26B A4B, 31B) support 256K tokens, while the smaller E2B and E4B support 128K tokens.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Incorrect — Gemma 4 12B does support up to 256K tokens of context.

name.text: TF: Removing encoders sacrifices audio quality

questiontext.text: Removing the dedicated audio encoder in Gemma 4 12B significantly worsens its audio recognition performance compared to the smaller E4B model.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Incorrect — Gemma 4 12B actually outperforms E4B on audio benchmarks (e.g. FLEURS word error rate of 0.069 vs 0.08), showing the encoder-free approach does not sacrifice audio quality.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Correct — despite removing the 305M-parameter audio encoder, Gemma 4 12B achieves better audio recognition scores than the encoder-based E4B model.
